papers.title: Beyond LLM Serving: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Workloads for Embodied AI System Design
papers.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models translate multimodal observations into low-level robot actions. During robot operation, each control period sets an inference deadline, and overruns leave the robot acting on stale observations, reducing task success. Meeting this deadline motivates on-device or nearby edge execution, where a single robot requires batch-1 inference outside the design point of LLM serving systems. papers.title: From Rewards to Consequences Through Designing AI
papers.summary: Reinforcement Learning (RL) can be introduced to K–12 learners through accessible examples of agents learning from rewards and interaction. However, such examples may leave deeper questions of AI design and critical AI literacy unexplored. This demo presents Reward Machine, a browser-based, GDPR-compliant, no-code classroom activity for learners aged 13–15 that introduces RL through game creation. Learners design their own story to be implemented in grid-world environments, define agents, goals, and reward structures, and compete to train agents in peer-created scenarios. papers.title: INTERACTIVE MELODY GENERATION AND ROBOTIC SAXOPHONE PERFORMANCE: THE ROBOSAX MELODY SLOT MACHINE
papers.summary: This paper presents RoboSax Melody Slot Machine, a system that combines Melody Slot Machine, a dial-based interface for exploring melodically coherent variations, with RoboSax, a robotic saxophone that automates fingering with servo motors. Selected melodies are transmitted as MIDI to RoboSax, while the performer supplies breath and articulation. Because the melodic variations are generated by a GTTM-based morphing method, users can explore related phrases without losing structural coherence. The system therefore supports both accessible melody creation and embodied wind-instrument performance

papers.title: TARMAC as a taxonomy for robot manipulation in chemistry
papers.summary: Abstract Laboratory automation has benefited substantially from well-defined protocols and machine-readable representations of chemical procedures. Yet a long tail of context-dependent physical tasks, including setup, adjustment, and cleanup, continues to require manual intervention or bespoke robotic implementations tailored to individual workflows and platforms. This study examines whether this apparent diversity can be organized into a structured and reusable action space. papers.summary: Embodied agents driven by vision-language models (VLMs) can describe a scene fluently and invent objects, attributes, relations or executable targets. Such errors may cause serious injury if the language response is translated into navigation or manipulation operations. papers.title: Towards a competence-behaviour-design alignment for educational robotics kits: a theoretical synthesis and development principles
papers.summary: Abstract Educational robotics kits (ERKs) are widely used to support competence-oriented technology education, yet their design is rarely grounded in clearly prioritised technological competences and associated learning behaviours. This research, situated in China’s General Technology curriculum, addresses this gap by developing a competence-behaviour-design (C-B-D) alignment for ERKs. The research problem concerns what consistent priority competences and their operationalised learning behaviours are required to guide ERK design. A two-phase mixed-methods approach was adopted. papers.summary: The primary aims of this study are to explore (i) what typical daily and long-term interactions between private robot owners and their robots look like (ii) what role online robotics communities play for social robot owners (iii) how and why users customize their robots (iv) how customization factors into continued robot usage (v) how robot customization behaviours are discussed, encouraged, and disseminated through online robotics spaces. papers.summary: Robotic disassembly must be considered during the product design phase to accelerate automated remanufacturing. However, designers currently lack quantitative feedback for identifying the structural elements that hinder robotic operations. To address this, this study proposes an analytical framework that provides actionable redesign guidance focused on fastener reduction, because fasteners are numerous and ubiquitous components found in almost all manufactured products. papers.summary: Dynamically processing mechanical signals is crucial for soft robotics and mechanosensing, where classical viscoelastic materials lack intrinsic tunability. papers.title: AirAlign: Geometry-Aware Relative Pose Alignment for UAV Last-Meter Navigation
papers.summary: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) navigation in modern low-altitude environments requires more accurate pose alignment in the final approach stage for target information acquisition or manipulation, making "last-meter" navigation increasingly important. However, severe viewpoint and appearance variations make this task challenging. To tackle this problem, we propose AirAlign, a framework for RGB-only image-pair relative pose alignment for UAVs. papers.summary: Large-scale Transformers have achieved remarkable success across NLP, computer vision, and robotics, but their growing computational and memory demands challenge efficient inference. papers.title: REAL-TIME DETECTION AND ANALYSIS OF VEHICLE SPEED BASED ON COMPUTER VISION TECHNOLOGIES
papers.summary: This paper proposes software for detecting and analyzing the speed of motor vehicles based on images obtained from video surveillance cameras. The system relies on computer vision methods: vehicles are detected using the YOLOv8 neural network, tracked across the frame sequence by the ByteTrack algorithm, and pixel coordinates are converted into real metric distances by means of a homography matrix. papers.summary: Conventional college fitness training in China relies on uniform schedules that ignore between-student variability, producing marginal gains for many and elevated risk for those pushed beyond their adaptive ceiling. papers.summary: Animals and humans use multiple behavioral strategies to perform tasks. papers.summary: Enterprise collaborative networks must reorganise as markets shift, partners fail and demand changes.
